title: Nucleic Acid Purification with Magnetic Beads
author: Opentrons
materials: Pick up tips from A1-H1 – position 7

steps.title: Set up deck
steps.instruction: Pause until told to resume and set the deck up as described in the SOP.

steps.title: Add magnetic beads to samples
steps.instruction: Dispense magnetic beads into every well of the sample plate on the magnetic module.

substeps.instruction: Move pipette to channel 1 of the reagent plate located in position 5.
Aspirate 20 µL of beads 3 mm from the bottom of the reagent well, mix by aspirating/dispensing 150 µL total volume twice, then create a 20 µL air gap.
Dispense the 20 µL bead suspension into wells A1–H1 of the sample plate 2 mm above the well top and blow out.
Repeat the aspirate‑dispense cycle for all columns so that every well receives beads.

steps.title: Incubate for bead binding
steps.instruction: Pause for 5 minutes to allow the beads to bind nucleic acids.

steps.title: Magnet incubation
steps.instruction: Pause for 3 minutes to let the beads migrate to the magnetic module.

steps.title: Remove supernatant
steps.instruction: Aspirate and discard the supernatant from each well.

substeps.instruction: Aspirate 40 µL of supernatant from wells A1–H1 on the magnetic module 2 mm from the bottom at a slow speed.
Dispense the aspirated liquid into the middle of the waste trough in position 1, 10 mm from the bottom, and blow out.
Eject the used tips back into the tip box located in position 2.
Repeat the aspirate‑dispense‑eject cycle for all columns of the plate.

steps.title: First ethanol wash
steps.instruction: Add ethanol wash buffer to all wells, then incubate briefly.

substeps.instruction: Move pipette to channel 3 of the reagent plate in position 5.
Aspirate 100 µL of wash buffer 3 mm from the bottom of the reagent well, then add a 20 µL air gap.
Dispense the 100 µL wash buffer into wells A1–H1 of the sample plate on the magnetic module 2 mm above the well top and blow out.
Repeat the aspirate‑dispense cycle for the entire plate.
Pause for 30 seconds at room temperature (RT) to allow the wash to act.

steps.title: Remove first wash
steps.instruction: Aspirate the first ethanol wash and discard it.

substeps.instruction: Aspirate 100 µL of wash buffer from wells A1–H1 on the magnetic module 2 mm from the bottom at a slow speed.
Dispense the aspirated liquid into the middle of the waste trough in position 1, 10 mm from the bottom, and blow out.
Eject the used tips back into the tip box in position 2.
Repeat the aspirate‑dispense‑eject cycle for all columns.

steps.title: Second ethanol wash
steps.instruction: Perform a second ethanol wash using the same volumes and timings.

substeps.instruction: Move pipette to channel 4 of the reagent plate in position 5.
Repeat the steps for adding wash buffer (aspirate 100 µL + 20 µL air gap, dispense into all wells, incubate 30 s at RT).
Repeat the steps for removing wash buffer (aspirate 100 µL, dispense to waste, eject tips) for the entire plate.

steps.title: Air‑dry pellet
steps.instruction: Pause for 10 minutes at room temperature to air‑dry the bead pellet.

steps.title: Add elution buffer
steps.instruction: Dispense elution buffer into each well and mix.

substeps.instruction: Move pipette to channel 5 of the reagent plate in position 5.
Dispense elution buffer into wells A1–H1 of the sample plate on the magnetic module 3 mm from the bottom.
Mix by aspirating and dispensing 10 µL of liquid five times, then blow out.
Repeat the dispense‑mix cycle for the entire plate.

steps.title: Elute nucleic acids
steps.instruction: Incubate the plate to release nucleic acids from the beads.

substeps.instruction: Pause for 10 minutes at room temperature.

steps.title: Magnet incubation before collection
steps.instruction: Pause for 2 minutes at room temperature to allow beads to re‑capture on the magnet.

steps.title: Transfer eluate to elution plate
steps.instruction: Collect the eluate from each well and transfer it to the elution plate.

substeps.instruction: Aspirate 20 µL of eluate from wells A1–H1 on the magnetic module 1 mm from the bottom.
Dispense the 20 µL into the corresponding wells A1–H1 of the elution plate located in position 3 and blow out.
Repeat the aspirate‑dispense cycle for all wells so that the entire eluate is transferred.
